root_cause.text: `ib_uverbs_post_send()` in the RDMA uverbs subsystem trusted the userspace-controlled `cmd.wqe_size` field and used it to `kmalloc()` a buffer that was later accessed as `struct ib_uverbs_send_wr` without validating that the size was at least the structure size, enabling out-of-bounds reads from undersized allocations.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (cmd.wqe_size < sizeof(struct ib_uverbs_send_wr)) return -EINVAL;` before `user_wr = kmalloc(cmd.wqe_size, GFP_KERNEL | __GFP_NOWARN);`, and the CVE text says the function previously used `cmd.wqe_size` “without any validation before passing it to kmalloc() and using the allocated buffer as struct ib_uverbs_send_wr,” causing reads of `user_wr->opcode`, `user_wr->num_sge`, and other fields beyond the allocated buffer.

intent_record.intent_summary: Reject undersized send work requests and avoid noisy allocation warnings in ib_uverbs_post_send.
intent_record.what: The code adds a size check that վերադարձs -EINVAL when cmd.wqe_size is smaller than sizeof(struct ib_uverbs_send_wr), and changes the kmalloc call to use GFP_KERNEL | __GFP_NOWARN instead of GFP_KERNEL.
intent_record.how: This prevents allocation and subsequent handling of an undersized work request buffer, avoiding invalid memory interpretation or access when the user-provided WQE size is too small. The __GFP_NOWARN flag also suppresses allocation failure warnings for this path.

grouping_result.intent: Reject undersized send work requests and avoid noisy allocation warnings in ib_uverbs_post_send.

relevance_review.reason: The change explicitly rejects undersized send work requests in ib_uverbs_post_send, which directly matches the root cause of trusting userspace-controlled wqe_size and allowing undersized allocations to be accessed as a larger struct.

candidates.rationale: This allocation directly trusts the user-controlled cmd.wqe_size without first ensuring it is at least sizeof(struct ib_uverbs_send_wr), allowing an undersized buffer that later gets accessed as a full send work request.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement allocates the send work request buffer using the user-controlled cmd.wqe_size without validating that it is large enough for struct ib_uverbs_send_wr, which can lead to later out-of-bounds reads from an undersized allocation in ib_uverbs_post_send().

commit 67cdb40ca444c09853ab4d8a41cf547ac26a4de4
Author: Roland Dreier <rolandd@cisco.com>
Date:   Fri Oct 14 15:26:04 2005 -0700

    [IB] uverbs: Implement more commands
    
    Add kernel support for userspace calling poll CQ, request CQ
    notification, post send, post receive, post SRQ receive, create AH and
    destroy AH commands.  These commands allow us to support userspace
    verbs for devices that can't perform these operations directly from
    userspace (eg the PathScale HCA).
bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct is explicitly guarded against in this version of ib_uverbs_post_send(). The function checks the userspace-provided size before allocating and before copying: `if (in_len < sizeof cmd + cmd.wqe_size * cmd.wr_count + cmd.sge_count * sizeof (struct ib_uverbs_sge)) return -EINVAL;` and, crucially, `if (cmd.wqe_size < sizeof (struct ib_uverbs_send_wr)) return -EINVAL;`. Because the root cause was trusting `cmd.wqe_size` and allowing an undersized allocation later accessed as `struct ib_uverbs_send_wr`, this snippet already contains the fix by rejecting `wqe_size` smaller than the structure size. Therefore the vulnerable construct is not present here, and the code is already fixed.
